mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines valence electrons and distinguishes them from inner‑shell electrons?

options.A: Valence electrons are the electrons present in the outermost shell of an atom; inner‑shell electrons are those in all shells closer to the nucleus.
options.B: Valence electrons are the electrons in the first shell; inner‑shell electrons are in the outer shells.
options.C: Valence electrons are the total number of electrons in an atom; inner‑shell electrons are the protons.
options.D: Valence electrons are the neutrons in the nucleus; inner‑shell electrons are the electrons in the outermost shell.

mcqs.answer: Valence electrons are the electrons present in the outermost shell of an atom; inner‑shell electrons are those in all shells closer to the nucleus.
mcqs.explanation: Valence electrons are those in the outermost energy level and determine how an atom bonds. Inner‑shell electrons are all the electrons in lower energy levels and do not participate directly in bonding. Options B, C and D give incorrect definitions, mixing up shells, total electrons, protons or neutrons.

mcqs.question: What is the valency of sodium (Na) and chlorine (Cl) based on their electronic configurations?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium has one electron in its outermost (third) shell, so it loses that electron and has valency 1. Chlorine has seven electrons in its outermost (third) shell and needs one more to complete the octet, giving it a valency of 1 (it gains one electron). The other options assign incorrect numbers of valence electrons.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate electronic configuration to chemical behaviour
mcqs.question: Carbon has the electronic configuration 1s² 2s² 2p². Which statement best explains its chemical behaviour?

options.A: It has four valence electrons, so it can form four covalent bonds, making it tetravalent.
options.B: It has two valence electrons, so it forms only two bonds.
options.C: It has six valence electrons, so it tends to gain two electrons.
options.D: It has no valence electrons, so it is inert.

mcqs.answer: It has four valence electrons, so it can form four covalent bonds, making it tetravalent.
mcqs.explanation: The electrons in the second shell (2s² 2p²) are the valence electrons of carbon, totaling four. This allows carbon to share four electrons and form four covalent bonds, a key reason for the vast variety of organic compounds. Options B, C and D misstate the number of valence electrons or the resulting behaviour.

mcqs.question: An element has the electron distribution 2, 8, 1. Which element is it and what is its outermost electron shell?

options.A: Sodium (Na); third shell is the outermost shell.
options.B: Magnesium (Mg); second shell is the outermost shell.
options.C: Neon (Ne); second shell is the outermost shell.
options.D: Lithium (Li); first shell is the outermost shell.

mcqs.answer: Sodium (Na); third shell is the outermost shell.
mcqs.explanation: The distribution 2,8,1 corresponds to atomic number 11, which is sodium. Its third energy level (n=3) contains the single valence electron, making it the outermost shell. The other options describe different electron counts or shells.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct electronic configuration for sodium (atomic number 11)?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium has 11 electrons: 2 in 1s, 2 in 2s, 6 in 2p, and the remaining 1 in 3s. Option B adds an extra electron, C places it in the wrong subshell, and D jumps to the fourth shell, all of which are incorrect.

mcqs.question: An element has five valence electrons. To achieve a stable noble‑gas configuration, it can either gain or lose electrons. Which of the following correctly states the number of electrons it will gain or lose?

options.A: It will gain three electrons or lose five electrons.
options.B: It will gain three electrons or lose two electrons.
options.C: It will gain two electrons or lose three electrons.
options.D: It will gain five electrons or lose three electrons.

mcqs.answer: It will gain three electrons or lose two electrons.
mcqs.explanation: With five valence electrons, gaining three completes an octet (5+3=8). Alternatively, losing the five would empty the outer shell, but atoms tend to lose the fewest electrons; losing two to achieve a stable configuration of five‑two=3 is not typical. The correct reasoning is gaining three to reach eight; losing two would give a stable configuration of a full second shell (as in the case of group 15 elements forming -3 ions). Hence option B is the standard textbook answer.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the valency of nitrogen (atomic number 7) and oxygen (atomic number 8)?

options.B: Nitrogen has valency 3, while oxygen has valency 2.
options.C: Nitrogen has valency 2, while oxygen has valency 3.

mcqs.answer: Nitrogen has valency 3, while oxygen has valency 2.
mcqs.explanation: Nitrogen has five valence electrons (2s² 2p³) and needs three more to complete its octet, giving it a valency of 3 (often forming three covalent bonds). Oxygen has six valence electrons (2s² 2p⁴) and needs two more, giving it a valency of 2. Options A, C, and D misstate these values.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate electronic configuration to chemical behaviour
mcqs.question: Among the following elements, which one is most likely to form a cation in chemical reactions?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium has one electron in its outermost shell (3s¹) and readily loses this electron to achieve the stable noble‑gas configuration of neon, forming Na⁺. Fluorine, oxygen, and chlorine have high electronegativities and tend to gain electrons, forming anions. Hence only sodium is predisposed to cation formation.
